_comment: INLINESYNC-1 — one entry per hand-synced SSOT/inline-copy pair. check-inline-ssot-sync.mjs reads this manifest and applies ONE general algorithm (per `mode`) to every pair, same doctrine as scripts/published-dirs.json driving regen-sitemap.mjs: generator/gate share one manifest so they can't drift apart independently. Do not hand-add a pair without also re-deriving its consumer count the way research/PROOFSYNC-GATE-SCOPE-1-2026-08-02.md and board row INLINESYNC-1 did.
_comment_codeOnly: INLINE-SSOT-PORTS-GATE-1 added mode `codeOnly` for whole-MODULE inline ports: a self-contained tool page cannot import, so the port strips `export` keywords and omits the module's section banners, and a byte-compare therefore fails on a CORRECT port (which is why `wholeFileBlock` could not express these pairs). A codeOnly pair names its consumer page plus the unique region markers delimiting the ported block; the gate compares both sides after removing ONLY comments, ES-module linkage and insignificant whitespace — never identifiers, numeric literals, string contents, operators or control flow. See the normalizer contract in check-inline-ssot-sync.mjs and the executable negative controls in check-inline-ssot-sync.fixtures.mjs (`--self-test`). A missing consumer file, or a missing/ambiguous region marker, is a FAILURE and never a silent pass (STANDING-ORDERS #34c). codeOnly pairs take NO baseline exception: after normalization a difference is by construction a code difference, and in a verifier that is the defect this mode exists to find.

pairs.label: OCG-PROOF v1 secured() helper (audit_signature.proof strip, incl. empty-object cleanup)
pairs.note: Single minified line, pasted (with or without the OCG-PROOF v1 header comment) into every page that signs/verifies a W3C Data Integrity proof. This exact function is the PROOFSYNC-SECURED-1 defect surface: the pre-fix text was missing the empty-audit_signature cleanup, so hashData() hashed a different shape on the verify path than the sign path and verification silently returned false.

pairs.label: OCG SIGN-VERDICT AFFORDANCE v1 module (securedRecord + SignVerdict.mount, whole file)
pairs.note: The SSOT's own header comment states the WHOLE FILE is 'hand-synced into each consuming tool page' -- the sync unit is the entire module, not just securedRecord(), so this pair uses wholeFileBlock mode instead of a single extracted line.

pairs.label: OCG-CANON v1 __ocgCanon() helper (RFC 8785/JCS recursive key-sort canonicalizer)
pairs._note_order: keep codeOnly pairs after the byte-compare pairs — purely cosmetic, the gate is order-independent.
pairs.note: The conceptual SSOT is chaingraph/kernels/_hash.mjs's cgCanon export, but _hash.mjs is an ES module (const arrow, export syntax) and can never be byte-identical to a global inline <script> function statement by construction. fix-hash-scheme.mjs's OCG_BLOCK is the repo's own existing, already-shipped transcription of that same algorithm into exactly this inline shape ('byte-equivalent to kernels/_hash.mjs and worker.mjs cgCanon' per its own comment, injected by that script's Scheme-A auto-fix) -- extracting the canonical line FROM that file (read-only, never edited by this gate) means this manifest carries zero hand-typed copies of the string itself and reuses the one generator the codebase already had for this exact shape, rather than re-deriving or re-typing a fourth copy.

pairs.label: _detmath deterministic-transcendental math bundle (whole inlinable body, pasted into RISC0-guest kernels)
pairs.trigger: /* ===== inlined _detmath (RISC0 guest provides only _hash; bundle import is unavailable in-guest) ===== */
pairs.note: ACCTINFRA-BUNDLE-DRIFT-GATE-1, closing ACCT-INFRA-KERNELS-BUILD-SPEC.md §4.2 (recorded fix shape: 'a fourth manifest pair in wholeFileBlock mode over chaingraph/kernels/*.kernel.mjs, with the consumer count re-derived rather than asserted' — adjudicated, Tim popup GO 2026-08-30). §4.1 rule 1 forbids importing the bundle at runtime because the RISC0 guest provides only _hash, so each consuming kernel pastes the bundle body inside the §4.1 sentinel comments (the pair trigger), and §4.1 rule 2 makes a byte-different copy a fork, i.e. the defect this pair gates (PROOFSYNC-SECURED-1 precedent, generalized from HTML page to guest kernel: a stale inline copy silently changes every execution_hash). ssotUntilMarker carves the unit at the GENERATED bundle's ES export tail because the composition contract itself replaces that tail with a per-kernel destructure when inlining (§4.1's recipe) — the tail is linkage, not payload, and byte-comparing it would red every correct consumer by construction. scanExt is '.kernel.mjs' because the consumers are kernels, not pages. Consumer count RE-DERIVED against current bytes at gate-build time (2026-08-31, git grep over the sentinel): FIVE full-paste consumers — art-211-prediction-market-analyzer, art-270-perp-funding-carry, art-273-pendle-yield, art-278-reputation-score-aggregator, art-356-compute-oprisk-sma-2026 — all verified byte-identical to the carved unit at registration. A SIXTH kernel, art-663-apy-earned-recompute, carries a SELF-DECLARED TRIMMED copy (its own header: 'exp + log only … Trimmed from _detmath.bundle.mjs'), landed after §4.2 measured five; a trim is a fork under §4.1 rule 2 and is NOT silently pinned as a baseline variant (this manifest's ratchet: no new hand-typed variant joins) — it is out of this pair's unit (its header differs, so the trigger does not fire) and was reported for adjudication in the ACCTINFRA-BUNDLE-DRIFT-GATE-1 check-off, not fixed here (gate row fence: no kernel/bundle content edits).

pairs.label: ICS23 declarative Merkle proof verifier (whole module, ported inline into tools/585)
pairs.note: ICS23-VERIFY-TOOL-1 ported this module's function bodies inline because a single self-contained page cannot import (CONTRACT §1.1, zero network calls after load), and verified the port byte-identical to the SSOT under a code-only diff at authoring time — with nothing mechanically holding it there afterwards. The module carries the VSA-2022-103 domain-separation fix (checkInnerAgainstSpec's leaf-prefix rejection plus the exact min/max prefix-length and child-size bounds), so a silent divergence here is a verifier that returns PASS on a forged proof the fixed module rejects. The region markers bracket exactly the ported block: the page's own banner says everything between them is the module, and the UI code after `End of the verbatim port` is deliberately outside the comparison because it is page-specific presentation, not verification logic. The port's `'use strict';` sits inside the startMarker rather than being normalized away — an ES module is implicitly strict and a script-context IIFE is not, so the directive is a real statement the module does not have, and excluding it by delimiter is honest where a normalizer rule would be a licence to ignore stray directives.

pairs.label: C2SP transparency-log verification primitives (whole module, ported inline into tools/625)
pairs.note: TOOLS625-SSOT-REPORT-1 resolved the divergence INLINE-SSOT-PORTS-GATE-1 measured and left unregistered (see git history for the removed `_unregistered_pending_adjudication` record): the page's byte helpers, RFC 6962 walk, parseSignedNote, formatCheckpoint and toCosignedData were a re-transcription, not a verbatim port (globalThis.crypto.subtle -> crypto.subtle, two added short-path `if (!p.length) return false;` guards in verifyInclusion, five template literals rewritten as string concatenation, a dropped trailing comma). Per Tim's 2026-08-15 ruling, the module's own error contract stays untouched (throw on a too-short sibling path, via an unguarded `p[0]` on an empty array) and the page re-ports it byte-verbatim instead: no consumer of c2sp-tlog-verify.mjs behaviour changed, because the module was not edited. runVerifier()'s existing outer try/catch is what absorbs that throw into a reported error for a person who pastes too few sibling hashes, so the short-path case is still handled — just by the page's own error boundary rather than a page-local return-false inside the ported block itself. Consumers of the module enumerated at registration time: scripts/register-sigsum.mjs, scripts/register-rekor.mjs (both CLI, not kernels), and chaingraph/kernels/c2sp-tlog-verify.test.mjs; no `.kernel.mjs` kernel imports this module, so no execution_hash is in scope.
